subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Gas Turbines: Power from Combustion
description: A quick win: understand Gas Turbines: Power from Combustion.

hook.text: Compress air, add fuel, ignite it, and spin a turbine. That's a jet engine.

buildup.text: The compressor squeezes incoming air. The combustor heats it intensely.

discovery.text: Hot expanding gas spins the turbine, which drives the compressor and output.

twist.text: Blades face 1,400°C — past their melting point. Internal cooling saves them.

climax.text: Gas turbines power jets, ships, and peak-load power plants worldwide.

punchline.text: Burn fuel, spin blades, make power. Simple idea, extreme engineering.

quiz.question: How do gas turbine blades survive temperatures above their melting point?
options: They are made from ceramics that don't melt
Internal cooling channels circulate cooler air through the blade
The blades spin so fast that heat can't build up
